A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Content can be reliably matched despite terminology changes and page reflow.

before.justification: v3 reports original policy-training experiments across five environments, RLHF win-rate evaluations, discriminator analyses, and ORPO ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results in Table 1, Figures 2–6, and Appendix E, including RLHF evaluations and ORPO ablations.

M1.justification: ORPO's discriminator objective, reward adjustment, and alternating discriminator/PPO updates remain unchanged in Section 6 and Appendix B. Renaming the base policy to the reference policy does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same traffic, pandemic, glucose, RLHF, and tomato-watering environments. The AlpacaFarm-based RLHF setup and Appendix E's AlpacaEval evaluation are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Appendix E retain the same AD, state-OM, and state-action-OM comparisons using chi-squared and KL divergences, together with the same reference-policy, unregularized, and true-reward baselines. RLHF-specific exclusions are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendices C–E preserve the coefficient sweeps, architectures, training budgets, held-out-prompt evaluation, reward metrics, and win-rate procedures. No experimental setting is substantively revised.

E4.justification: The coefficient-sensitivity analysis in Figure 5, discriminator-accuracy analysis in Figure 6, and training-order and reward-clipping ablations in Appendix E.3 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds, medians and standard deviations in result tables, and seed ranges in Figure 5 and Table 4. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Table 1 and Appendix E's Tables 4–10, plotted results, and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 4 retains median RLHF win rates of 52.83 for chi-squared regularization and 51.50 for KL.

T1.justification: Definitions 4.1–4.2, Theorem 5.1, and the appendix results and proofs are mathematically unchanged. The return–occupancy identity moves from v3 Equation (3) to v4 Equation (8) in Appendix A.1; this is relocation, not new theory.

C1.justification: The principal definition, guarantee, and empirical advantage claims remain. However, v4 removes Section 2's explicit claim to be the first application of occupancy-measure regularization to reward hacking and instead emphasizes specific distinctions from prior definitions in Section 4.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations for OM versus AD and chi-squared versus KL, qualifications concerning guaranteed improvement, and limitations of the RLHF true-reward model remain unchanged. Appendix interpretations of discriminator accuracy and ablation robustness are also retained.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D retain the same implementation details, architectures, hyperparameters, clipping procedure, trimmed-mean estimator, and RLHF implementation information. The abstract provides the same code-access link.

R1.justification: v4 adds Fluri et al. (2024), Kwa et al. (2024), and Skalse et al. (2024). Sections 2–4 revise the comparison with earlier reward-hacking definitions and replace the broad priority claim with more specific positioning.

P1.justification: v4 renames the base policy to the reference policy, streamlines passages in Sections 1–4, explicitly lists the two existing desiderata, and reorganizes discussion of prior definitions. It also retitles Definition 4.2, relocates an equation to Appendix A, and adds an equal-contribution note.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their substantive displays, with updated policy labels and limited caption edits. ICLR publication headers and page reflow change presentation, including moving Table 5 onto Appendix E's opening page.

improvement.justification: v4 improves clarity and scholarly context by explicitly organizing the definition's desiderata and comparing it with additional related formulations, while moderating the broad priority claim. Some introductory explanations are shortened, but the technical material and experimental evidence remain available. The overall gain is limited to exposition and positioning.
